close_reason: Done. Added '# Panics' rustdoc section to extract_response (client.rs:874) documenting that T's Deserialize panics propagate: 'This function does not catch panics from T's serde::Deserialize implementation. If a custom T type's deserialize impl panics — e.g. because of an .unwrap() on a sub-field — the panic propagates through extract_response to the caller's await point. description:
client.rs:614-646 — pub fn extract_response<T: serde::de::DeserializeOwned>

The function calls `T::deserialize(&inv.1)` at line 645. If T's Deserialize impl panics (e.g., a user-defined struct whose deserialize calls .unwrap() on a sub-field), the panic propagates up through extract_response and out to the caller's await point.

The doc-comment promises:
"Returns ClientError::MethodNotFound if no invocation with the given call_id exists. Returns ClientError::MethodError if any invocation with the matching call_id is a JMAP 'error' response."

It does NOT promise that the function is panic-free. For a public foundation library, callers may reasonably assume:
- "All errors return Err" — false if their T panics
- "Calling this in a join handle won't crash the runtime" — false

This is mostly a documentation gap. The function's behavior is correct (it propagates T's panics, which is the right thing — T's contract is the caller's responsibility). But the doc-comment doesn't say so.

Recommendation: add to the doc-comment: "Panics: this function does not catch panics from T's Deserialize implementation. Custom T types whose deserialize may panic will propagate the panic to the caller."

Same applies to JmapRequestBuilder::add_call where args: serde_json::Value can be constructed by the caller — if the caller passes a Value that resulted from a panic-on-conversion, the panic happens at construction time before reaching this crate. Less of an issue.

Low priority. Documentation fix only.
title: extract_response<T> panic on T's deserialize boundary undocumented — what if T's impl panics
